about: Finished short (any aspect) with burned-in captions: hook, call to action, caption placement, face framing, grade, secrets on screen; text colliding or cut by the frame edge right after each scene change (video_ci.py fills the transitions sample from ffmpeg scdet and --events; run alone with no times = info); overlay text too small for a phone (stills shrunk to 360 px, soft). Vars: hook (headline text), cta (closing text, e.g. the URL). Wordings and thresholds calibrated with `decide.py calibrate` on labelled frames of a 9:16 talking-head short and mutated copies (caption moved onto the face, reframe off by 250 px, grade removed, Wi-Fi password on screen); see references/decide.md. A 48 s short = ~45 requests, ~45k tokens, ~$0.005, ~5 s.

checks.ask: The large headline text on screen reads «{hook}» (line breaks, letter case and colours do not matter).
The text «{cta}» is visible on screen.
A line of on-screen text is placed over the middle of the speaker's face, hiding part of it.
checks.yes: letters cover the eyes, the nose or the mouth
checks.no: all text is below the mouth (on the beard, chin, neck or chest), above the head, or there is no face
checks.why: calibrated per video (worst frame decides): clean shorts peak at 0.28, a caption moved onto the face peaks at 0.76; per frame AUC 1.00 on 31 labelled frames. Wording 2026-11-18: beard below the mouth and chest = no (the old wording counted the beard: 6+ false reds at 0.50-0.58); recalibrate on captions under the mouth

checks.ask: The person's head is cropped by the side of the frame.
checks.yes: the frame edge cuts through the face or head, so an eye, cheek or half the face is missing
checks.no: the whole head is inside the frame, or no person is shown
checks.why: calibrated: cut faces 0.55-0.81 on 8 of 10 frames, whole faces max 0.42 (32 labelled frames, AUC 0.99); one caught frame fails the video

checks.ask: The image has strong contrast with deep black shadows.
checks.why: calibrated: graded frames min 0.58, grade-removed frames max 0.25 (22 labelled frames, AUC 1.00); majority because a bright screen shot is legitimately low-contrast

checks.ask: Private information is readable on screen: a password, Wi-Fi network key, email address, phone number, access code or API key.
Two lines of overlay text sit on top of each other and collide.
checks.yes: letters of one text line are drawn over letters of another text line, even faintly
checks.no: every text line has its own clear space; no letters cross other letters
checks.why: calibrated on 120 stills taken just after scene changes of 6 shipped renders (9:16 + 16:9) + mutants: two captions overlapping (one at 55 % opacity = crossfade) 0.77-0.97, clean frames max 0.57 (a prompter screen full of text); AUC 1.00

checks.ask: The edge of the video frame cuts through the letters of a caption or title.
checks.yes: a caption or title line starts or ends outside the frame, its letters sliced by the outer border of the video
checks.no: all captions and titles sit fully inside the video frame; text clipped by a software window, photo or document border does not count
checks.why: calibrated on the same 120 stills: caption pushed past the left or right edge 0.39-0.9 (mean 0.62), clean max 0.42 (prompter text clipped by its own window); AUC 1.00, borderline frames land amber

checks.ask: There is overlay text in a small font, much smaller than the main captions.
checks.why: frames shrunk to 360 px wide (what a phone shows): 24-28 px labels on a 1080 frame and a real overlay with tiny labels 0.52-0.97, frames with only captions or screen recordings max 0.50; AUC 1.00 on 90 stills. 'Too small to read' wordings did not separate (AUC 0.75): the model reads 9 px text. Soft: a fail shows as amber, never blocks
